tldr: This paper proves the constant-factor all-regime pure-central-private precision frontier for the oracle mean outcome under optimal individualized treatment in an author-defined categorical randomized-trial benchmark. For every allowed sample size, category count and privacy budget, the explicit numerical rates satisfy \(\mathfrak R\asymp R_\star\) and \(\mathfrak L\asymp L_\star=\sqrt{R_\star}\), where the second objective is worst-case expected length of a connected interval with uniform finite-sample coverage at least \(0.9\). Public branch rules give total computable attaining releases that satisfy pure replacement privacy on every dataset. Legal fixed-pair priors prove the converses in the original confidential-record experiment. The results include the matched sparse frontier, the dense localized certificate, strong-privacy saturation and necessary and sufficient consistency conditions for arbitrary public sequences.
gap: Existing optimal-value inference, nonsmooth property estimation and private testing provide separate ingredients. None of the opened results identifies the uniform fixed-pair pure-private frontier with honest connected intervals on the complete stated causal experiment.
fill: The focal outputs are numerical sample, dimension and privacy rates, total computable attaining releases, mechanism-uniform converses and necessary and sufficient consistency conditions. The proof obligations retain the original causal experiment and unconditional privacy at every occupancy.
